hook.text: Every network—roads, friendships, the internet—is just dots and lines. Nodes hold things. Edges connect them.

buildup.text: Graph theory formalized this: a network is a set of nodes (vertices) connected by edges (links).

discovery.text: The structure of connections determines how information flows. Dense networks spread information fast.

twist.text: Not all connections are equal. Weighted edges carry different capacities, like roads carrying different traffic volumes.

climax.text: From neurons to the internet, the same graph abstractions describe every information network in nature and technology.

punchline.text: Dots and lines. Every network reduces to the same math.

quiz.question: What are the two basic elements of any network?
